title: Shinnecock (Neck, Bay, Hills, and Plain)
summary: Shinnecock is a major eastern Long Island placename associated with the Shinnecock people, Shinnecock plain, Shinnecock Hills, Shinnecock Bay, and the reservation.
introduction_content: Shinnecock is a Southampton placename attached to a neck of land, bay, range of hills, and to the Shinnecock people whose reservation remains there.
history_content: The name is rooted in the Shinnecock plain, where early Southampton colonists encountered Shinnecock people in 1640. Later English usage extended the name to the hills, bay, canal, and reservation landscape.
translation_content:
Recorded forms include Shunnecock, Shinecock, and Shinnacock. The name is interpreted as level land or level country, while the source argues against dividing the word as Shinnec-ock.

Why Place Names Matter

“It’s important to think about the histories of place names, to appreciate where they come from, what they mean, and what they can teach us about our environment.”

— Kaleigh Bradley, What’s in a Name? Place Names, History, and Colonialism (2015), Article opening
preservation_content: Shinnecock is not only a historical placename; it remains the name of a living Native Nation and homeland. The broad map marker is only a general placename reference, not a boundary for Shinnecock lands.
